questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: She has been suffering __________ fever for three days.
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is 'suffer from' (a disease/illness). 'With' is wrong — 'suffer with' is non-standard in this context; 'by' is wrong — it doesn't collocate with 'suffer'; 'of' is wrong — 'suffer of' is not grammatically correct in English.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: SAARC was established in which year and in which city?
questions.explanation: SAARC was established at the first summit held in Dhaka, Bangladesh on 8 December 1985. 1983/New Delhi is wrong — only a preparatory meeting occurred in 1983; 1987/Kathmandu is wrong — the secretariat was set up there but not founded then; 1990/Colombo is wrong — incorrect year and city.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A train travels 360 km in 6 hours. What is its speed in m/s?
questions.explanation: Speed = 360/6 = 60 km/h. Converting: 60 × 5/18 = 16.67 m/s. 15.67 m/s is wrong (converts 56.4 km/h); 17.67 m/s is wrong (converts 63.6 km/h); 18.67 m/s is wrong (converts 67.2 km/h).

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about phishing:

(i) Phishing involves sending fraudulent emails to trick users into revealing personal data.
(ii) Phishing websites often imitate legitimate banking or shopping sites.
(iii) Phishing attacks can only occur through email.
(iv) Users should verify website URLs before entering sensitive information.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Phishing uses fraudulent emails (i-correct), imitates legitimate sites (ii-correct), and verifying URLs is a protective measure (iv-correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because phishing also occurs via SMS (smishing), phone calls (vishing), and social media — not only email.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Gulmarg Gondola cable car system takes tourists up to which peak in its second phase?
questions.explanation: The Gulmarg Gondola Phase 2 takes visitors to Apharwat Peak at about 4,200 m. Kolahoi Peak is wrong — it is near Pahalgam; Haramukh Peak is wrong — it is in Ganderbal; Pir Panjal Peak is wrong — it is a range name, not the gondola destination.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Identify the type of clause in the sentence: 'I don't know WHETHER HE WILL COME.'
questions.explanation: 'Whether he will come' functions as the object of the verb 'know', making it a noun clause. An adjective clause is wrong — it would modify a noun; an adverb clause of condition is wrong — 'whether' here doesn't set a condition for the main verb; a main clause is wrong — it is subordinate.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When two trains move in opposite directions, their relative speed equals the sum of their individual speeds.
Reason (R): Objects moving towards each other close the gap faster than if only one were moving.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Relative speed in opposite directions = sum of speeds (A is correct). Because both are closing the gap simultaneously, the closing rate is their combined speeds (R is correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains the physics behind A; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are member countries of ASEAN?

(i) Indonesia
(ii) India
(iii) Vietnam
(iv) Philippines

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Indonesia (i-correct, founding member), Vietnam (iii-correct, joined 1995), and Philippines (iv-correct, founding member) are ASEAN members. India (ii) is wrong because India is a Dialogue Partner of ASEAN, not a full member.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the following idioms with their meanings:

Column I:
(a) To hit the nail on the head
(b) A bolt from the blue
(c) To cry over spilt milk
(d) To make hay while the sun shines

Column II:
(i) To regret something that cannot be undone
(ii) To say exactly the right thing
(iii) To take advantage of a good opportunity
(iv) A complete surprise or shock

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 'Hit the nail on the head' = say exactly right (a-ii); 'a bolt from the blue' = sudden surprise (b-iv); 'cry over spilt milk' = regret the irreversible (c-i); 'make hay while the sun shines' = seize opportunity (d-iii). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b); Option 3 swaps (c) and (d); Option 4 swaps (b) and (c).

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: The full form of 'HTTPS' is:
questions.explanation: HTTPS stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure — encrypting data between browser and server. 'Protocol System' is wrong — it ends with 'Secure'; 'High Transfer' is wrong — it starts with 'HyperText'; 'Transmission Protocol' is wrong — the correct word is 'Transfer'.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A boat travels 48 km downstream in 4 hours and returns upstream in 6 hours. The speed of the stream is:
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 48/4 = 12 km/h. Upstream speed = 48/6 = 8 km/h. Speed of stream = (12−8)/2 = 2 km/h. 1 km/h is wrong (uses wrong formula); 3 km/h is wrong (uses 12−8 = 4 then divides wrong); 4 km/h is wrong (takes difference without dividing by 2).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA):

(i) It was established to promote trade among ASEAN member nations.
(ii) AFTA aims to reduce tariff and non-tariff barriers.
(iii) India is a member of AFTA.
(iv) AFTA was signed in 1992.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: AFTA promotes trade among ASEAN members (i-correct), reduces tariff barriers (ii-correct), and was signed in 1992 (iv-correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because India is not a member of AFTA — it has a separate ASEAN-India FTA (AIFTA).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Pahalgam is called the 'Valley of Shepherds'.
Reason (R): The name Pahalgam is derived from the word 'Pahalgam' meaning shepherd's village, and the area has traditionally been home to Gujjar-Bakerwal shepherds.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Pahalgam is indeed called Valley of Shepherds (A is correct). The name's etymology and the presence of pastoral communities explain this title (R is correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains the origin of the name; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'reticent':
questions.explanation: 'Reticent' means unwilling to speak freely; reserved/taciturn. 'Talkative' is wrong — it's the antonym; 'Aggressive' is wrong — it means hostile/forceful; 'Generous' is wrong — it means willing to give.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the distances and speeds of four runners:

A → 200, 25
B → 200, 22
C → 200, 28
D → 200, 24

Arrange the runners in order of DECREASING speed:
questions.explanation: For same distance, lower time = higher speed. Speeds: B=200/22=9.09, D=200/24=8.33, A=200/25=8.0, C=200/28=7.14. Decreasing order: B > D > A > C. Option 2 is alphabetical order; Option 3 is increasing speed order; Option 4 incorrectly places A before D.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are types of malware?

(i) Virus
(ii) Worm
(iii) Firewall
(iv) Trojan Horse

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Viruses (i-correct), worms (ii-correct), and Trojan horses (iv-correct) are all types of malware. Firewall (iii) is wrong because a firewall is a security tool that PROTECTS against malware — it is not malware itself.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the sentence that contains an adverb clause of reason:
options: He ran so fast that he won the race.
She stayed home because she was ill.
If it rains, we will cancel the trip.
Although he is rich, he is humble.
questions.correctAnswer: She stayed home because she was ill.
questions.explanation: 'Because she was ill' gives the REASON for staying home — adverb clause of reason. 'So fast that' is wrong — it's result; 'If it rains' is wrong — it's condition; 'Although he is rich' is wrong — it's concession.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The headquarters of the International Labour Organization (ILO) is located in:
questions.explanation: ILO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. New York is wrong — it hosts the UN HQ; Paris is wrong — it hosts UNESCO; Vienna is wrong — it hosts IAEA.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about average speed:

(i) Average speed = Total distance / Total time.
(ii) For a round trip with equal distances at speeds 40 km/h and 60 km/h, average speed = 48 km/h.
(iii) Average speed is always the arithmetic mean of all speeds.
(iv) For equal distances, average speed = 2ab/(a+b).

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance/total time (i-correct); for equal distances at 40 and 60: 2×40×60/100 = 48 km/h (ii-correct); formula for equal distances is 2ab/(a+b) (iv-correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because average speed is the arithmetic mean only when TIME intervals are equal, not always.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Vaishno Devi shrine is located in which district of J&K?
questions.explanation: Vaishno Devi shrine is in the Trikuta Mountains of Reasi district. Jammu is wrong — it's the nearest city but different district; Udhampur is wrong — Reasi was carved from it; Kathua is wrong — it's a separate southern district.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the antonym of 'ephemeral':
questions.explanation: 'Ephemeral' means lasting a very short time; its antonym is 'permanent' (lasting forever). 'Brief' is wrong — it's a synonym; 'Temporary' is wrong — it's similar in meaning; 'Fragile' is wrong — it means easily broken, unrelated.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A strong password should contain a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters.
Reason (R): Complex passwords are harder to crack by brute-force attacks because they exponentially increase the number of possible combinations.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Strong passwords should mix character types (A is correct). This complexity exponentially increases possible combinations, making brute-force cracking impractical (R is correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains why A is important; Option 3 is wrong because R is technically accurate; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following international organizations with their founding years:

Column I:
(a) SAARC
(b) ASEAN
(c) United Nations
(d) European Union

Column II:
(i) 1945
(ii) 1967
(iii) 1985
(iv) 1993

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: SAARC was founded in 1985 (a-iii); ASEAN in 1967 (b-ii); UN in 1945 (c-i); EU (Maastricht Treaty) in 1993 (d-iv). Option 2 swaps SAARC and ASEAN years; Option 3 swaps UN and EU; Option 4 assigns EU year to SAARC.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A car travels the first half of a journey at 30 km/h and the second half at 50 km/h. The average speed for the entire journey is:
questions.explanation: For equal distances: Average speed = 2×30×50/(30+50) = 3000/80 = 37.5 km/h. 38.5 km/h is wrong (calculation error); 40.0 km/h is wrong (arithmetic mean of 30 and 50); 42.5 km/h is wrong (incorrect formula).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the homophone pair 'stationary' and 'stationery':

(i) 'Stationary' means not moving or fixed in position.
(ii) 'Stationery' refers to writing materials like paper and pens.
(iii) Both words have the same spelling.
(iv) 'Stationary' is an adjective while 'stationery' is a noun.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: 'Stationary' means immobile (i-correct); 'stationery' means writing supplies (ii-correct); 'stationary' is an adjective and 'stationery' is a noun (iv-correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because they have DIFFERENT spellings — 'stationary' ends in '-ary' and 'stationery' ends in '-ery'.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: If a man walks at 6 km/h, he reaches his destination 20 minutes early. If he walks at 4 km/h, he reaches 10 minutes late. The distance to the destination is __________ km.
questions.explanation: Let distance = d. Time difference = 20 + 10 = 30 min = 1/2 hour. d/4 − d/6 = 1/2. (3d − 2d)/12 = 1/2. d/12 = 1/2. d = 6 km. 4 km is wrong (gives time diff of 1/3 hour); 5 km is wrong (gives 5/12 hour); 8 km is wrong (gives 2/3 hour).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) came into effect in which year?
questions.explanation: SAFTA came into force on 1 January 2006. 2004 is wrong — that's when it was signed; 2008 is wrong — trade liberalization was already underway; 2010 is wrong — unrelated to SAFTA's start.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: The idiom 'to let sleeping dogs lie' means:
options: To wake up early in the morning
To avoid disturbing a situation that might cause problems
To be lazy and not work
To take care of pet animals
questions.correctAnswer: To avoid disturbing a situation that might cause problems
questions.explanation: 'Let sleeping dogs lie' means don't interfere with something that's currently not causing trouble. 'Wake up early' is wrong — literal misinterpretation; 'be lazy' is wrong — unrelated to the idiom's meaning; 'care for pets' is wrong — literal interpretation of words.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about data backup:

(i) A backup creates a copy of important data for recovery in case of loss.
(ii) Cloud storage is one method of backup.
(iii) Backups protect against ransomware attacks by providing clean copies.
(iv) Data backup is unnecessary if antivirus software is installed.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Backups create recovery copies (i-correct), cloud is a backup method (ii-correct), and backups protect against ransomware (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because antivirus can't prevent all threats — backups are still essential as a last line of defense against data loss.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Mughal Gardens located in Srinagar?

(i) Shalimar Bagh
(ii) Nishat Bagh
(iii) Chasma Shahi
(iv) Indira Gandhi Tulip Garden

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Shalimar Bagh (Jahangir), Nishat Bagh (Asif Khan), and Chasma Shahi (Shah Jahan) are all Mughal-era gardens (i, ii, iii correct). The Tulip Garden (iv) is wrong because it is a modern garden established in 2007, not a Mughal creation.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the sentence 'That he won the race surprised everyone', 'That he won the race' is a noun clause.
Reason (R): It functions as the subject of the verb 'surprised'.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: 'That he won the race' is a noun clause (A is correct). It functions as the subject (R is correct and this grammatical function is what makes it a noun clause). Option 2 is wrong because R explains exactly why it's a noun clause; Option 3 is wrong because R is correct; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: Two trains running in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h cross each other in 10 seconds. If the first train is 100 m long, the length of the second train is:
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 54 + 36 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Total distance = speed × time = 25 × 10 = 250 m. Length of second train = 250 − 100 = 150 m. 125 m is wrong (uses 22.5 m/s); 140 m is wrong (uses 24 m/s); 160 m is wrong (uses 26 m/s).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Act East Policy' of India (formerly 'Look East Policy') aims to strengthen India's ties with:
questions.explanation: India's Act East Policy focuses on deepening ties with ASEAN and the broader East Asian region. EU is wrong — India has separate engagement; SAARC is wrong — those are South Asian neighbours; African Union is wrong — India engages separately through India-Africa summits.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence using the past perfect tense:
options: She has finished her work before the guests arrived.
She had finished her work before the guests arrived.
She finished her work before the guests had arrived.
She was finishing her work before the guests arrived.
questions.correctAnswer: She had finished her work before the guests arrived.
questions.explanation: Past perfect ('had finished') is used for an action completed BEFORE another past action ('arrived'). Option 1 is wrong — 'has finished' is present perfect; Option 3 is wrong — the past perfect should be on the earlier action; Option 4 is wrong — 'was finishing' is past continuous, implying ongoing action.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Match the following cyber security terms with their definitions:

Column I:
(a) Firewall
(b) Encryption
(c) Keylogger
(d) Two-factor authentication

Column II:
(i) Records every keystroke to capture passwords
(ii) Requires two forms of verification for login
(iii) Monitors and filters network traffic
(iv) Converts data into unreadable coded format

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Firewall monitors/filters traffic (a-iii); encryption converts data to unreadable form (b-iv); keylogger records keystrokes (c-i); 2FA requires two verification forms (d-ii). Option 2 swaps firewall and encryption; Option 3 swaps keylogger and 2FA; Option 4 swaps encryption and keylogger.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A man walking at 5 km/h covers a certain distance in 6 hours. How long will it take him to cover the same distance by cycling at 15 km/h?
questions.explanation: Distance = 5 × 6 = 30 km. Time by cycling = 30/15 = 2 hours. 1.5 hours is wrong (uses 20 km/h); 2.5 hours is wrong (uses 12 km/h); 3 hours is wrong (uses 10 km/h).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about BIMSTEC:

(i) It stands for Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation.
(ii) Its secretariat is located in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
(iii) India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Thailand, and Myanmar are members.
(iv) It was established to replace SAARC.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: BIMSTEC's full form is correct (i-correct), secretariat is in Dhaka (ii-correct), and the countries listed are all members (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because BIMSTEC was not established to replace SAARC — it is a separate organization focusing on Bay of Bengal countries.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following sentences correctly uses the adjective clause?

(i) The man whom I spoke to was the manager.
(ii) I like the cake who was baked yesterday.
(iii) The city where we live is beautiful.
(iv) She wore the dress which her mother gifted.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: 'Whom I spoke to' correctly modifies 'man' (i-correct); 'where we live' correctly modifies 'city' (iii-correct); 'which her mother gifted' correctly modifies 'dress' (iv-correct). Statement (ii) is wrong because 'who' is used for people, not things — 'cake' should use 'that' or 'which'.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A train 200 m long takes 20 seconds to cross a platform 300 m long.
Reason (R): The train must cover a total distance equal to its own length plus the platform length, i.e., 500 m.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: A 200 m train crossing a 300 m platform at 25 m/s (500/20) takes 20 s (A is correct, given a speed of 90 km/h). The total distance is 200+300=500 m (R is correct and explains why crossing takes the time stated). Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains the calculation; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct; Option 4 is wrong because A can be correct at appropriate speed.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The SAARC secretariat is located in __________, Nepal.
questions.explanation: The SAARC Secretariat has been located in Kathmandu, Nepal since 1987. Pokhara is wrong — it's a tourist city; Biratnagar is wrong — it's an industrial city; Lumbini is wrong — it's Buddha's birthplace, a religious site.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct article: My neighbour is __________ European who has lived here for ten years.
questions.explanation: 'European' begins with a consonant sound /j/ (like 'yoo-'), so 'a' is correct. 'An' is wrong — used before vowel sounds; 'the' is wrong — the person is being introduced for the first time (indefinite); 'no article' is wrong — an article is needed before a singular countable noun.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: A computer worm differs from a virus because a worm:
options: Needs a host program to spread
Can replicate and spread independently without a host program
questions.correctAnswer: Can replicate and spread independently without a host program
questions.explanation: A worm self-replicates and spreads across networks without needing a host file. 'Needs a host' is wrong — that describes a virus, not a worm; 'cannot spread across networks' is wrong — worms specifically exploit networks to spread; 'only affects hardware' is wrong — worms target software/OS.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the journey of a bus on different road segments:

1 → 60, 40
2 → 90, 60
3 → 50, 50

What is the average speed for the entire journey?
questions.explanation: Total distance = 60+90+50 = 200 km. Total time = 60/40 + 90/60 + 50/50 = 1.5 + 1.5 + 1 = 4 hours. Average speed = 200/4 = 50 km/h. 48 km/h is wrong (miscalculates time); 49 km/h is wrong (arithmetic error); 51 km/h is wrong (wrong total distance or time).

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: The word 'bear' is a homonym because it can mean:
options: Both a large animal AND to carry/tolerate — same spelling, different meanings
questions.correctAnswer: Both a large animal AND to carry/tolerate — same spelling, different meanings
questions.explanation: 'Bear' has multiple unrelated meanings with the same spelling (noun: animal; verb: to carry/tolerate), making it a homonym. 'Only an animal' is wrong — it also means to carry; 'Only to carry' is wrong — it also means the animal; 'a bird' is wrong — bear is not a bird.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is a founding member of SAARC but not a member of ASEAN.
Reason (R): SAARC comprises South Asian nations while ASEAN comprises Southeast Asian nations, and India is geographically in South Asia.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: India co-founded SAARC and is not an ASEAN member (A is correct). The geographical basis — SAARC is South Asian, ASEAN Southeast Asian — explains India's membership pattern (R is correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains A; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following J&K tourist destinations with their famous features:

Column I:
(a) Dal Lake
(b) Gulmarg
(c) Sonamarg
(d) Patnitop

Column II:
(i) Hill station on Jammu-Srinagar highway
(ii) Gateway to Ladakh via Zoji La
(iii) Houseboats and shikaras
(iv) Skiing and Gondola cable car

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Dal Lake is famous for houseboats/shikaras (a-iii); Gulmarg for skiing/gondola (b-iv); Sonamarg is gateway to Ladakh via Zoji La (c-ii); Patnitop is a hill station on NH-44 (d-i). Option 2 swaps Dal Lake and Gulmarg; Option 3 swaps Sonamarg and Patnitop; Option 4 swaps Gulmarg and Sonamarg.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: The teacher is angry __________ the students for not completing their homework.
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is 'angry with' (a person). 'On' is wrong — 'angry on' is not standard English; 'at' is wrong — 'angry at' is used for situations, not people in formal English; 'upon' is wrong — 'angry upon' is not a valid collocation.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correct about converting units of speed?

(i) 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s
(ii) 1 m/s = 18/5 km/h
(iii) 54 km/h = 15 m/s
(iv) 20 m/s = 54 km/h

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s (i-correct); 1 m/s = 18/5 km/h (ii-correct); 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h, not 54 km/h.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: The purpose of a CAPTCHA on websites is to:
options: Verify that the user is a human and not an automated bot
Speed up the website loading process
Block all advertisements on the page
questions.correctAnswer: Verify that the user is a human and not an automated bot
questions.explanation: CAPTCHA distinguishes humans from bots to prevent automated spam/abuse. 'Encrypt data' is wrong — that's SSL/TLS; 'speed up loading' is wrong — CAPTCHA adds a step; 'block ads' is wrong — that's an ad blocker function.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The ASEAN-India Free Trade Agreement (AIFTA) on trade in goods came into effect in which year?
questions.explanation: AIFTA (Trade in Goods) came into effect on 1 January 2010. 2008 is wrong — that was the framework signing; 2012 is wrong — services and investment agreements came later; 2014 is wrong — unrelated to AIFTA implementation.
